checks: Compile/source representation; paired syntax only, no runtime route execution
cost: O(JSON bytes+rows) per page plus full page JSON memory; no cycle detection or finite page limit, so token cycles permit unbounded requests. Network latency dominates and is unmeasured.
description: list creates output and header, sends paginated JSON requests with encoded prefix/token, emits items in page order, sums parsed string sizes, and continues exactly while nextPageToken is a nonempty string.
forward: list creates output and header, sends paginated JSON requests with encoded prefix/token, emits items in page order, sums parsed string sizes, and continues exactly while nextPageToken is a nonempty string.
inverse: HTTP error cannot yield item rows for that response; parsing occurs only after successful text. Output/header can already exist when first request fails. Listing does not download object content.
For observed TSV, compatible JSON pages may have arbitrary unselected fields and page boundaries; size 0 can arise from '0', absent, nonstring or malformed size. Token history is lost.
limitations: No network/DNS/download, real catalog/corpus/model/teacher or database execution. Effect paths are source-derived; finite helper tests are not universal verification. No executable percentage surrogate or speed claim; future caps require metric/domain/reference and remain 1/2/5/10%.
state: Absent/nonarray items emit no rows. Missing or nonstring sizes become zero. Output is a prefix on request/parse/write failure. Counters require no overflow for this arithmetic model; bucket is interpolated without encoding.
